title: A local Noetherian ring with geometrically normal formal fibres has universally catenary henselization and is itself universally catenary when unibranch
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement says that a Noetherian local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres has universally catenary henselization, and that the ring itself is universally catenary when it is unibranch (statement lines 32497-32509). The proof is a two-step transfer of branch counts: the geometrically normal hypothesis makes the number of branches of the ring and of its completion agree, the branch-count criterion then gives the uniqueness of the minimal prime of the completion of the henselization modulo any of its minimal primes, which is precisely formal catenarity and hence universal catenarity by the Ratliff criterion; in the unibranch case the uniqueness of the minimal prime is transferred to the ring itself and the same criterion is applied again (proof lines 32511-32523). The transfer of the branch count through the henselization is the device that makes both assertions follow from one computation. The counted statement contains the author's reference environment, which the retained preamble typesets as a comment, so its citation is discarded and no bibliography is needed; the three same-chapter references are carried as navigation stubs.
